before.title: Admitted lines
before.body: один час — один час. два часа — два часа.

after.title: Start with the construction
after.body: These basic counting examples use nominative phrases. The related noun-case pattern also applies in inanimate accusative contexts, with the appropriate noun form. Other sentence cases require numeral declension as well as noun declension. A count ending in one outside the teen exception uses a nominative singular noun in the shown basic phrases. один час — один час. два часа — два часа.

before.title: Admitted instruction
before.body: Numerals larger than twenty follow the above rules using the last digit.

after.title: Two, three and four
after.body: A count ending in two, three or four outside the teen exception uses a genitive singular noun in the basic construction. This is a grammatical singular form even though the count is greater than one.

before.title: Admitted lines
before.body: пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.

after.title: Genitive plural counts
after.body: Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.

after.body: For a compound count, inspect the last two digits first. If they are 11, 12, 13 or 14, use genitive plural for the counted noun in the basic construction. Otherwise, the final digit selects the pattern: one, two-through-four, or zero/five-through-nine. after.title: Review the complete counted-noun rules

These basic counting examples use nominative phrases. The related noun-case pattern also applies in inanimate accusative contexts, with the appropriate noun form. Other sentence cases require numeral declension as well as noun declension. A count ending in one outside the teen exception uses a nominative singular noun in the shown basic phrases. один час — один час. два часа — два часа. 

A count ending in two, three or four outside the teen exception uses a genitive singular noun in the basic construction. This is a grammatical singular form even though the count is greater than one.

Counts ending in zero or five through nine use genitive plural in the basic construction. The teen exception also uses genitive plural. Ten and sixteen therefore fit this pattern. пять часов — пять часов. двадцать один час — двадцать один час.

after.title: A sentence outside the basic pattern
after.body: The I saw two friends sentence has an animate accusative object. Both the numeral and noun are declined; do not classify it with the basic nominative/inanimate accusative rule.
